findings.text: Under OBBBA, a solar project with COD after 2029 forfeits the 30% ITC unless physical-work beginning-of-construction was documented by July 4, 2026 — a deadline that has already passed. The dossier provides no BOC evidence, no COD, and no capacity. This is the single largest go/no-go item.

findings.title: Likely federal land / gen-tie crossing → NEPA + ROW, multi-year
findings.text: Trinity County is dominated by Shasta-Trinity National Forest and Trinity Alps Wilderness. Any gen-tie crossing federal land requires a BLM ROW grant, NEPA review, and plan conformance — precedent runs 2–3 years and is appeal-prone. Parcel ownership and gen-tie route are unverified.

findings.title: Timberland Conversion Permit likely required (forested parcel)
findings.text: Trinity County is heavily forested. Converting timberland to solar requires a Timberland Conversion Permit under the Z'berg-Nejedly Forest Practice Act — a distinct, lengthy, and often-contested approval not present in the dossier. Parcel vegetation/land-use class is unverified.

findings.title: Zoning district unverified — potential solar prohibition in rural/forestry districts
findings.text: Trinity County's zoning for parcel 025-340-12-00 could not be confirmed (county planning/assessor pages returned 404). Rural forested counties commonly restrict or prohibit commercial solar in timber/agriculture districts. If prohibited, the only viable path is CEC Opt-In (≥50 MW + ≥200 MWh), which preempts local zoning.

recommendedActions: Site control secured with legal description and acreage.
Zoning confirmed to allow solar+storage, or CEC Opt-In eligibility established.
BOC evidence provided and verified for ITC/PTC.
Interconnection study completed with acceptable cost and timeline.
Offtake agreement executed or credible path to offtake.
